description:
## Why

`pkix-lint-cabf` ships CA/B Forum lint bundles as "reference / not authoritative" interpretations — CA/B Forum publishes only PDFs, so any machine-readable encoding is somebody's interpretation. The dominant ecosystem interpretations are:

- **zlint** (Go, Apache-2.0) — maintained by Let's Encrypt + community. The de facto reference everyone in the CA world cross-checks against. Source: <https://github.com/zmap/zlint>.
- **pkilint** (Python, Apache-2.0) — maintained by DigiCert. Strong on S/MIME BR and ETSI / EU Trust List concerns. Source: <https://github.com/digicert/pkilint>.

If `pkix-lint-cabf`'s interpretations silently diverge from both zlint and pkilint, that's a defect surface. Differential cross-checking earns the "useful even if not authoritative" label.

## What

Add zlint and pkilint as differential oracles to `pkix-difftest`, scoped to the CA/B Forum lint domain (NOT general path validation — that stays on OpenSSL + pyca).

Architecture (parallels the existing oracle layout at `pkix-difftest/python/pyca_oracle.py`):

1. **zlint sidecar.** Either:
   - **Subprocess**: spawn `zlint -format json <cert.der>` per cert, parse the JSON output. Requires zlint binary in PATH or vendored under `pkix-difftest/bin/`.
   - **Python wrapper**: install `zlint` via `pip install zlint` (the Python bindings package), call from a sidecar script analogous to `pyca_oracle.py`.

   First option is simpler. Second is more portable but adds a Python dep.

2. **pkilint sidecar.** New `pkix-difftest/python/pkilint_oracle.py` that uses `pkilint.cabf_serverauth` (TLS BR) and `pkilint.cabf_smime` (S/MIME BR) APIs.

3. **Verdict reconciliation.** Each oracle emits a list of finding IDs. `pkix-difftest` classifies per cert:
   - **Agreement**: all three (pkix-lint-cabf, zlint, pkilint) emit the same finding set (or all clean).
   - **PkixStricter**: pkix-lint-cabf emits findings the others don't.
   - **PkixLaxer**: zlint or pkilint emits findings pkix-lint-cabf doesn't.
   - **Disagree**: oracles diverge among themselves (zlint says X, pkilint says Y); pkix verdict is documented but not flagged as wrong.

4. **Test corpus.** Reuse the bettertls / x509-limbo corpora plus dedicated CA/B Forum BR test vectors. May need to source these from zlint's own test fixtures (which are Apache-2.0 and citable).

5. **Baseline + CI.** Generate `pkix-difftest/baseline-cabf-lint.{json,md}` on every push. Treat divergence increases as warnings, not failures (since both oracles can also be wrong).

## Acceptance

- [ ] zlint oracle integration (subprocess or Python wrapper).
- [ ] pkilint oracle integration.
- [ ] Verdict reconciliation logic.
- [ ] CA/B Forum BR test corpus (sourced from zlint fixtures or curated).
- [ ] Baseline output committed under `pkix-difftest/baseline-cabf-lint.{json,md}`.
- [ ] CI run on every push.
- [ ] Analysis MD documenting where pkix-lint-cabf diverges from zlint / pkilint and why (intentional vs unintentional).

## Out of scope

- Replacing zlint or pkilint. They keep doing their thing. We just cross-check against them.
- Wholesale adoption of zlint's lint catalog as `pkix-lint-cabf`'s catalog — that's a separate proposal (see related-to PKIX-XXXX if/when filed).
- Using zlint / pkilint as path-validation oracles (their domain is lint, not chain walking).

## Depends on

- `PKIX-amgn.5` (substantive `pkix-lint-cabf` content exists to cross-check). Without that, there's nothing to compare.

## Related to

- `PKIX-hbzo` (`pkix-difftest` completeness umbrella).
- `PKIX-8qz1` (per-rule split — fast Rust executes, OSCAL describes; cross-validation confirms the executable side matches consensus).

## Filed by

Surfaced in conversation 2026-05-11 after noting CA/B Forum publishes only PDFs; zlint and pkilint are the de facto machine-readable interpretations, so they're the natural cross-validation oracles.
title: pkix-difftest: zlint + pkilint as cross-validation oracles for pkix-lint-cabf
